project.name: poc-27-recursive-self-improvement
project.description: POC 27: asks how much of embabel-smith's improvement loop can be made self-referential — can the process that builds be improved, including the part that does the improving, without grading its own homework. The loop in the studio improves only the prompts of the steps that failed and cannot touch the generator that wrote them, and a builder-built pack is stamped with a baseline equal to its own build-time score, so the strict gate comparison can never pass. This POC fixes an interpreter (the Embabel platform, the scorer, the frozen task set, the labelled trace corpus) and mutates only artifacts that interpreter runs: generated agent specs, generated JavaScript skill scripts run through POC 26's GraalJS engine, and a generated improvement policy expressed as one of those scripts. Improvement is measured as a derivative across at least two generations against a noise floor recorded before any tuning, and every variant is kept in an archive rather than hill-climbed.
